newsitem.title: USA: Minn. airports panel plans to lengthen two runways.
newsitem.headline: Minn. airports panel plans to lengthen two runways.

text.p: Metropolitan Airports Commission is expected to approve later this month a $13 million project for runway extensions at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport for new nonstop Northwest Airlines Corp service to Hong Kong, the deputy executive director of planning and environment said Tuesday.
One runway would be extended temporarily in 1998 for the construction of a permanent extension of another runway during the construction season in 2000, Nigel Finney said.
The airport's longest runway at 11,000 feet is still too short to meet Northwest's needs, Finney said.
Plans call for adding 1,000 feet to an even shorter runway to meet basic needs while putting another 1,000 feet on the longest runway, Finney said.
Northwest requested the extension to make non-stop service from the Twin Cities to Hong Kong more economically feasible, spokeswoman Marta Laughlin said.
Northwest hopes to start the run in the fall on a reduced capacity if possible, Laughlin said.
Because of weight limits and the length of the flight, Northwest cannot book 60 passenger spaces on the flights in order to take off from the shorter runways, Laughlin said.
Finney said an airports commission committee approved the concept at its last meeting and is expected to make a formal recommendation to the commission Tuesday for its meeting July 21.
Commission staff must prepare an environmental assessment report on the extension plans for the Federal Aviation Administration, Finney said.
FAA could order an environmental impact statement on the project or determine that its minimal impact warrants no further inquiry, Finney said.
